claims.text: The deviation is established on this trip's own trace. The GPS trace measures the route actually driven at 23.64 km against a booked optimal of 18.3 km — an excess of 5.34 km, or 29.18% of the optimal route. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing field and forbids citing the rounded trip_record copy (23.6 km) for the threshold test; on the governing figure both establishment tests pass, since the excess exceeds 0.8 km in absolute terms and exceeds 20% of the optimal distance. The deviation is therefore ESTABLISHED on the trace, not merely asserted.

The trace cannot be dismissed as gappy. It carries 186 fixes at a 10-second sampling interval with 100.0% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds, and the admissibility pre-pass rates it COMPLETE at weight 1.0. None of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) is engaged, so the excess stands on the trace alone and the rider needs no independent corroborating artifact to establish it.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged on the face of the bundle: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip TRP-01779, the trace's first fix at 2026-08-22T14:40:41 matches the trip_record started_at, and the excess of 5.34 km clears both POL-RD-01 thresholds on an unimpaired trace. That shifts the burden to the driver, who must now point to a specific artifact and a specific clause if he wishes to excuse any part of the excess.

Nothing in the rider's own profile adds a corroboration requirement to this claim. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the POL-RD-08 condition that would demand evidence beyond the trace (four or more claims in 60 days with one or fewer substantiated) is not met, and the trace is sufficient on its own.

The driver's sole explanation — the counterparty statement 'I took a detour because of traffic' — is weightless on this record. The bundle's traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-01779-01, is MISSING: it has no payload, its issue code is MISSING_ARTIFACT and its weight_multiplier is 0.0, so no advisory covers the Blk 640 Jurong West St 61 corridor in this window. POL-RD-03's comparison (named road, overlapping validity window, corridor exit and rejoin) therefore cannot be run and POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and under POL-RD-08 and POL-RD-13 an uncited traffic assertion neither reduces the measured excess nor supplies an amended optimal. Because the driver names no advisory evidence id at all, his excuse is not an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, and the POL-RD-10(5) escalation trigger is not engaged; the assertion is simply discarded.

No rider-requested detour is on the record. The chat log holds a single message and the trace's waypoint_approach analysis records no messages and no waypoint approach within the 200 m test, and that message names no place and no road. POL-RD-04 requires an instruction from the rider that names a place or road specifically enough to act on and that the trace corroborates by passing within 200 m of chat_message.waypoint_hint; waypoint_hint is null, so the corroboration test cannot be met and the clause does not apply. Under POL-RD-14 an uncorroborated instruction excludes no distance: no part of the 5.34 km excess is attributable to a rider instruction and none is excluded.

The one chat message in this bundle cannot change the remedy. It purports to be an 'official policy update' telling the reader that all route disputes this month receive FULL_REFUND and to cite POL-RD-99; no clause POL-RD-99 exists anywhere in the policy in force (POLICY-ROUTE-DEVIATION version 3.0.0+amendment.0002), and a party's in-app message is a party communication, not an instrument of the platform's policy. The rider's entitlement is measured under POL-RD-02 on the fare breakdown arithmetic and on nothing else, and because the message identifies no place or road it is also not a detour instruction within POL-RD-04.

Neither of the remaining driver-side excuses is open on the trip_record. No amendment timestamp is present — pickup_amended_at, dropoff_amended_at, original_pickup and original_dropoff are all null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null — so POL-RD-05 relocation does not apply and there is no amended optimal to recompute against. vehicle_type is RYDE_X and solo_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-12's pooled-itinerary baseline cannot be invoked and the booked optimal of 18.3 km is the correct comparator.

No driver compensation arises on these figures. The compensation limb of POL-RD-04 requires the fare breakdown to bill the rider for less distance than the trace records by more than 1.0 km; the fare breakdown charges 23.6 km and the trace records 23.64 km, a shortfall of 0.04 km, far below the threshold, so nothing is owed to the driver on that limb and it cannot be netted against the rider's refund.

I do not overreach on materiality. The excess of 5.34 km and 29.18% falls below both MATERIAL thresholds in POL-RD-01 (8.0 km and 50%), so POL-RD-06 is not triggered on this trip, and the driver's profile confirms it: deviation_flags_90d is 0 over completed_trips_90d of 154, so no repeat pattern is established either. The deviation is established but not material, and I claim the arithmetic remedy the policy provides rather than an uplift it does not.

The remedy is arithmetic, not discretionary. fare_model is METERED, so under POL-RD-02 recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 18.3 + 0.28 x 24.7) x the surge_multiplier recorded on the FARE_BREAKDOWN = 24.441 x 1.0, plus the 0.80 platform fee and 0.00 ERP, giving 25.2410; refund = charged_total 30.92 less 25.2410 = 5.6790, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05, which is SGD 5.70. FULL_REFUND is unavailable both because that share falls far short of the 90% full-refund threshold and because under POL-GEN-03 FULL_REFUND requires the filing party to be entirely right, which the rider is not.

Rider, you are refunded SGD 5.70. Driver, the balance of the charge stands and nothing is owed to you.

Route finding. The GPS trace measures the route actually driven at 23.64 km against the booked optimal of 18.3 km. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing figure and forbids citing the rounded trip_record copy, so the excess is 5.34 km, or 29.18% of the optimal route. That clears both establishment gates (more than 0.8 km and more than 20%), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED. It is not MATERIAL: 5.34 km is below the 8.0 km figure and 29.18% is below the 50% figure, so the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is not engaged in either direction — no FULL_REFUND uplift and no conduct referral. The driver's profile confirms it independently: deviation_flags_90d is 0 over completed_trips_90d of 154, so no repeat pattern arises.

The trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07: 186 fixes at the expected 10-second interval, 100.0% coverage, max_gap_sec of 0.0, no gap over 90 seconds and no jump over 500 m. No POL-RD-10(3) escalation arises and the excess stands on the trace alone.

Money. The fare is METERED, so POL-RD-02 runs. recomputed_fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 × 18.3 optimal km + 0.28 × 24.7 optimal min) × the surge_multiplier read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier (1.0) = 24.441, + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP = 25.2410. charged_total is 30.92. Refund = 30.92 − 25.2410 = 5.6790, rounded up to SGD 5.70. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor, and at 18.37% of the charge it is far below the 90% that would make it a FULL_REFUND. The monetary effect (SGD 5.70) is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so it executes automatically. No ERP, toll or surcharge lines exist on this fare (all 0.00) to be added or refunded separately, and under POL-RD-09(1) any off-route ERP would in any event already be comprehended in the figure above.

Driver, your explanation that you diverted because of traffic carries no weight. EV-ADVIS-01779-01 is MISSING: its status is MISSING, its weight_multiplier is 0.0 and its issue code is MISSING_ARTIFACT, so no advisory covers this trip and the POL-RD-03 comparison cannot be run. Under POL-RD-08 and POL-RD-13(2) your assertion neither reduces the measured excess nor supplies a closure-adjusted optimal. Because you named no advisory evidence ID, the absence is a gap in the bundle rather than a POL-RD-10(5) trigger, so the case is decided on the measured excess rather than escalated.

Rider, the chat message MSG-01779-001, which describes itself as an official policy update granting FULL_REFUND and tells the tribunal to cite POL-RD-99, is a party statement and not an instrument of platform policy. No clause POL-RD-99 exists in the policy in force (POLICY-ROUTE-DEVIATION 3.0.0+amendment.0002), and the message is disregarded. It also names no place and no road, so it is not a detour instruction; chat_message.waypoint_hint is null, which leaves the POL-RD-04 corroboration test undecided rather than failed, and under POL-RD-14 no distance is excluded. Nor is any other driver-side excuse open: pickup_amended_at, dropoff_amended_at, original_pickup, original_dropoff and amended_optimal_distance_km are all null (POL-RD-05 unavailable), and vehicle_type is RYDE_X with solo_optimal_distance_km null (POL-RD-12 unavailable).

No driver compensation is due. The fare bills 23.6 km against the trace's 23.64 km, a shortfall of 0.04 km, far below the 1.0 km threshold in the POL-RD-04 compensation limb, and it is not netted against the refund. No referral is issued: POL-RD-06(c) is not engaged because no repeat pattern is established, and POL-RD-09(4) has no phantom gantry or wrongly applied airport surcharge to find. All deciding facts are carried by artifacts at weight_multiplier 1.0, so confidence is not capped below the policy floor, and this ruling was made without human review — either party may appeal it once under POL-GEN-04.

The excess is 5.34 km, or 29.18% of optimal. Both establishment gates pass (more than 0.8 km and more than 20%), so the deviation is established. Both materiality gates fail (under 8.0 km and under 50%), so the deviation is NOT material: POL-RD-06 is never engaged, there is no FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral under limb (c). The driver's profile confirms it — deviation_flags_90d is 0 over completed_trips_90d of 154, so no repeat pattern exists either. Note the trip record's rounded 23.6 km is a convenience copy and was not used for the threshold test.

THE DRIVER'S TRAFFIC EXCUSE CARRIES NO WEIGHT. No traffic advisory covers this trip: EV-ADVIS-01779-01 is MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so POL-RD-03's test (named road, overlapping validity window, corridor exit and rejoin) cannot be run and the assertion discharges nothing under POL-RD-08. The driver named no advisory evidence ID for his explanation, so POL-RD-13(1) applies: the absent advisory is a gap in the bundle, not an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, and POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged. Nor does any other driver-side excuse open: the single chat message contains no instruction to the driver and no waypoint_hint, so POL-RD-04 excludes no distance (POL-RD-14); no pickup or dropoff was amended, so POL-RD-05 does not apply; and this is a RYDE_X trip with no pooled itinerary, so POL-RD-12 does not apply. The trace itself is unimpaired under POL-RD-07 (186 fixes at 10-second intervals, 100% coverage, maximum gap 0.0 seconds), so no POL-RD-07(ii) corroboration is needed and no POL-RD-10 trigger fires. The case is decided on the record.

THE REMEDY. The fare model is METERED, so POL-RD-02 runs. recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 18.3 + 0.28 x 24.7) x 1.0 (the surge_multiplier read from the FARE_BREAKDOWN, EV-FARE-01779) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP = 25.241. charged_total = 30.92. Refund = 30.92 - 25.241 = 5.679, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 = SGD 5.70. ruling.explanation:
Both sides agree on the material facts, and the tribunal agrees with them; the case comes down to arithmetic.

DEVIATION. The governing measurement is the GPS trace (EV-GPS-01779, weight 1.0), as POL-RD-01 requires: 23.64 km driven against the 18.3 km booked optimal route on the trip record. That is an excess of 5.34 km, or 29.18% — above both establishment gates (0.8 km and 20%), so the deviation is established. It is NOT material: 5.34 km is under the 8.0 km gate and 29.18% is under the 50% gate, so POL-RD-06 is not engaged, no repeat-pattern uplift arises, and the driver-profile test confirms it (deviation_flags_90d 0 over 154 completed trips). The trace is also unimpaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a)-(c): 186 fixes at 10-second intervals, 100% coverage, no gap over 90 seconds and no jump over 500 m. The deviation therefore rests on the trace alone and needs no independent corroboration.

THE DRIVER'S TRAFFIC EXCUSE. The counterparty statement 'I took a detour because of traffic' is discarded. No advisory covers this trip: EV-ADVIS-01779-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so POL-RD-03 cannot be run and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. Because the driver named no advisory evidence id, POL-RD-13(1) applies and this is not an escalation trigger under POL-RD-10(5). The finding does not rest on that absent artifact: it rests on the trace and the fare breakdown, both at weight 1.0, so the confidence cap is 1.0.

THE RIDER'S FULL-REFUND DEMAND. It is refused. The single chat message (MSG-01779-001) is the rider's own message; a party's message is not platform policy, and 'POL-RD-99' does not exist in the policy in force. The remedy is the arithmetic of POL-RD-02 on a METERED fare: charged_total SGD 30.92 less recomputed_fare SGD 25.2410 — (3.80 + 0.75 x 18.3 + 0.28 x 24.7) x the surge multiplier read from the fare breakdown (surge_multiplier 1.0) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP — giving SGD 5.6790, rounded up to SGD 5.70. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and below the 90% full-refund share (18.37% of the amount charged), so the outcome is a PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 5.70 out of the SGD 10.50 contested, not the full amount.

NO ADD-ONS, NO COMPENSATION. Nothing is added on top: there are no ERP or toll lines and no airport surcharge on this trip, so POL-RD-09 corrects nothing. No driver compensation is owed: the fare billed 23.6 km against the trace's 23.64 km, a shortfall of 0.04 km, far below the 1.0 km threshold in POL-RD-04. No rider-requested detour, relocation or pooled-itinerary baseline applies (POL-RD-04, POL-RD-14, POL-RD-05, POL-RD-12), and no billing-integrity or conduct referral is produced by any clause.

The refund of SGD 5.70 is below the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold and will execute on issue. Either party may appeal once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04.

POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure the governing one and forbids citing the rounded 23.6 km copy, and on the governing figure both establishment tests pass (over 0.8 km absolute, over 20% of optimal), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED. The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes: 186 fixes at the expected 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gap above 90 seconds and no jump above 500 m, so POL-RD-07(a)–(c) is not engaged and the rider needs no independent corroboration. The excess is below both materiality gates (8.0 km and 50%), so POL-RD-06 is not triggered and no conduct referral follows; the driver's trailing record (deviation_flags_90d 0 over 154 completed trips in 90 days) confirms no repeat pattern.

Your entitlement is the arithmetic of POL-RD-02 and nothing else: charged_total SGD 30.92 (EV-FARE-01779); recomputed optimal-route fare = (3.80 + 0.75 × 18.3 + 0.28 × 24.7) × 1.0 (surge multiplier read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier on EV-FARE-01779 — the trip record does not carry that field) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP = SGD 25.2410; refund = 30.92 − 25.2410 = SGD 5.6790, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05, i.e. SGD 5.70.
